### The market: what creators ask for

# Creator survey: what would make Frame Job a leading creator editor

## Summary

This survey is dated 1 November 2026. It asks what would make Frame Job a leading editor for content creators. It draws on five inputs:

- an inventory of the tree;
- four research sweeps (creator tools, pro editors, screen and tutorial tools, creator demand);
- three strategists' proposals;
- the candidates merged from those proposals;
- adversarial checks of each candidate against the code, Apple's frameworks and the market.

Frame Job is already ahead of most creator tools on finishing: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs, and an MCP surface that covers the whole editor. It loses creators earlier, at the jobs that now define a creator editor:

- cutting a talk by its transcript;
- polishing a screen recording from the cursor;
- turning a horizontal edit into vertical shorts;
- finding the clips worth posting;
- switching podcast angles by speaker;
- cutting the presenter out of the background.

Agent access no longer sets a tool apart, because most AI-forward editors gained an MCP server in 2026. No rival combines what Frame Job has: a full editor whose every edit is a pure, undoable op, analysis that runs on the creator's Mac, and AI on the creator's own key with no credits.

The recommendation is to ship those creator jobs as on-device commands whose results land as ordinary edits on the timeline, in the order below. The rest is either table stakes to pick up later or not worth chasing.

## What Frame Job has

Frame Job is a native macOS editor for Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. It is a Swift/AppKit app over a Rust core, Apache-2.0, with no account and no backend. As of 1 November 2026 it has the following.

- **Editing.** One kind of track. Move, trim, slip, roll, rate-stretch, split, lift, ripple delete, insert and overwrite. Nests. Picture and sound linked for J- and L-cuts. Markers with a chapter flag. A second preview window. Every edit is one undo step through one mutation point, and a refused edit says why in the rule's own sentence.
- **Picture.** Transform, crop, blend modes, chroma key, spotlight, obscure regions, text with reveals, shapes with gradients, blurred backgrounds, and matte tracks that let any clip cut the track behind it. Actions animate almost every property, including speed, which is how speed ramps work. 13 transitions, and Zoom to Region for screencasts.
- **Audio.**
  - A per-clip chain: voice isolation, EQ, hum and noise reduction, gate, a phrase-level leveller, de-esser, compressor and true-peak limiter.
  - Enhance Voice, Match Audio, Normalize to LUFS, Duck by Speech, and Synchronize Audio with drift correction.
  - Track compressor and limiter, a live loudness meter, stems, and a −1 dBTP master on every export.
- **Clean-up.** Remove Silences (on-device Silero VAD), Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI word timings; cloud-only), and `get_transcript`. The Assistant cuts false starts when asked.
- **Captions.** On-device or AssemblyAI transcription. Subtitles plus five word-by-word styles and three looks. SRT and WebVTT export; SRT import.
- **Colour and HDR.**
  - Grading: wheels, curves, hue curves, looks, .cube LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, and four scopes.
  - Log footage: Apple Log (detected on import), S-Log3, V-Log and Canon log.
  - HDR: HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR deliverables, on a 16-bit float compositor.
- **Graphics.** Sandboxed JavaScript modules that return SVG per frame, 23 bundled templates, shareable `.fjgraphic` packages, and agents that write new graphics.
- **Recording.** A display or a window through ScreenCaptureKit, with system audio, a separate microphone file, click rings, pause and resume, a camera beside the screen (bottom-right), and voice-over.
- **Export.** H.264, HEVC (10-bit and with alpha), AV1 and VP9 through bundled encoders, ProRes, audio formats and stems, GIF, APNG and stills. An Export Queue, embedded chapters, and loudness targets of −14 and −16 LUFS.
- **Agents.** 106 product tools over a local socket (one per edit, plus app-state tools), the bundled `framejob-mcp` helper, and `render_frame` so an agent can look at its work. An in-app Assistant runs on the creator's own Anthropic key and shows its spend.

### Checked absent or partial

| Feature | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A transcript view where deleting words cuts the video | Absent | Cutting by transcript works only through the Assistant or MCP (`get_transcript` + `ripple_delete_ranges`). |
| Cursor, click and key events from recordings | Absent | `RecordingSetup.swift` sets `showsCursor` and `showMouseClicks`, so the pointer is burned into the picture and no events are stored. |
| Auto-reframe, subject tracking | Absent | `set_canvas` fits or letterboxes. There is no Vision import in `app/Sources`. A spec §1 non-goal. |
| Finding clips in long recordings | Absent | Nothing in the code or the guide. |
| Speaker-based angle switching, multicam | Absent | A spec §1 non-goal. Only the first audio track of a file is read (`CompositionBuilder.firstTrack`, `core/src/container.rs`). |
| Background removal without a green screen | Absent | Issue #124 is iceboxed. The recorded camera is fixed bottom-right (spec §11 CAM-10). |
| Placing part of a file, a source viewer | Absent | `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` take only track, media and position. |
| Proxies | Absent | Playback at 60 fps is checked on a 1080p movie (`docs/manual-checks.md` PB-2), and a few 4K rows exist. There is no multi-stream 4K or multi-hour figure. |
| Saved text and caption styles, brand kit, project templates | Absent | Four hard-coded text presets (`TextPane.swift`). Word-style colours can be set only by an agent. |
| Platform presets, safe-zone overlays, chapter-list text, thumbnail preset | Partial | Loudness targets and a vertical canvas preset exist. Named platforms, overlays and chapter text do not. |
| Translation, soft subtitle tracks, WebVTT import | Absent | |
| Stock media, direct upload, collaboration, cloud sync | Absent | |
| Eye contact, text-to-speech, beat detection, stabilisation, motion blur, optical-flow retiming | Absent | Several are spec §1 non-goals; beat detection is candidate #415. |

The in-app tutorials (TU0–TU3) are on an unmerged branch, and the owner's trial (TU4) is still owed.

### Where it is already ahead

- The whole editor is exposed as MCP tools printed from the core's own op table. Every agent edit is an undo step shown live, and `render_frame` lets an agent check its work.
- Its audio chain is deeper than any creator tool surveyed: a leveller, de-esser, true-peak master, LUFS targets, stems, Synchronize Audio with drift correction, and Duck by Speech.
- Colour management and HDR deliverables (HLG, HDR10, an SDR version) and log support. Creator tools lack these.
- Codec breadth: AV1 and VP9 with bundled encoders, VP9 and HEVC with alpha, ProRes 4444, and WebM and MKV import without re-encoding.
- A programmable motion-graphics engine whose templates agents can write.
- Open source with bring-your-own key and on-device processing first: no credits, no subscription, no upload of footage.

## The market in late 2026

Status words follow the vendor's own: shipped; beta (including open beta, public beta and research preview); announced. Where a claim rests on third-party coverage or on a vendor's own marketing, the text says so. Source tags such as [C1] refer to the Sources section.

### Creator tools
### Screen and tutorial tools

Camera cutout (beta), layouts, face tracking, LUTs (4.0). Privacy masking (4.1, shipped). MCP server (announced, in progress). | About $29 a month, subscription only. The lifetime licence was withdrawn in October 2025. | [S1] [S2] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S6] [S7] |

What changed:

- **The category rests on cursor data.** The pointer and click events are captured apart from the frames [S2] [S3] [S19] [S16].
- **Auto zoom grew** typing triggers, spring motion and lenses [S18] [S19] [S16] [S4].
- **Presenter-camera cutout, layouts and face tracking** shipped across the leaders in September and October 2026 [S6] [S16] [S11] [S19] [S13].
- **Every recorder now has an agent surface**, but most only manage recordings [S16] [S14]. Tella's agent edits the timeline in public beta [S12]. ScreenKite claims 83 editing tools [S22].
- **Subscription pricing drew a backlash** [S7] [D19], and free or lifetime alternatives grew [S23] [S17] [S21].

### What creators ask for

- **Editing is the biggest time sink.** One vendor classified 27,555 comments on 44 creator-education channels. Editing and production was the largest category, at 21.4% of actionable comments, ahead of monetisation at 15.6% [D1]. This is one vendor's analysis, not a survey.
- **Most work alone, and repurposing is wanted.** In Adobe Express's survey of 384 US video creators (December 2025), 86% work solo. The most-wanted new AI features were auto-repurposing (19%), instant platform-specific edits (14%) and help while filming (14%) [D2].
- **AI use is near-universal, but cost and training worry them.** In Adobe's 2025 Creators' Toolkit (more than 16,000 creators, 8 countries), 86% use generative AI. High cost is the top barrier, at 38%, and 69% worry their content will train AI without permission [D3].
- **They want control over agents.** In Adobe's 2026 report, 85% say the final decision must stay with the creator. Among creators who want more agent independence, 44% want to review, edit or undo at any point, and 37% want to see what the agent is doing and why. 57% say AI output usually needs moderate or extensive editing [D4]. Epidemic Sound found 94% use AI and 89% feel pressure to [D5].
- **Video podcasts are big and the picture edit is still manual.**
  - YouTube reports over 1 billion monthly podcast users [D10]. Spotify says more than 500 million users have streamed a video podcast [D11]. Edison found 57% of Americans 12+ have both listened to and watched a podcast [D12].
  - Automatic angle switching has long-open Premiere idea threads [D13] and is sold as AutoPod for about $29 a month [D14].
  - Descript users ask for multicam export to Final Cut Pro and Premiere (181 votes) [D6].
- **Descript frustrations.** The top requests are regenerating speech in more languages (753 votes), an iOS/iPadOS app (417), transcription in more languages (400) and strip silence (192) [D6]. Reviewers report slow scrubbing and long exports [D8]. Plans moved to media minutes plus AI credits with no rollover [D7].
- **Captions.** Premiere's animated-caption request has about 416 votes, and users round-trip to CapCut [D15]. A verifier counted about 380. Either way, the request is for animated word captions, which Frame Job already has.
- **Auto-cutters are distrusted.** Riverside Magic Clips is faulted for cutting where a thought ends rather than where the energy peaks [D16]. Gling sometimes cuts good takes [D17].
- **What makes creators switch tools:**
  - price rises and forced subscriptions [C5] [D19] [S7];
  - content-licence scares [D18];
  - stability regressions [D20];
  - metered AI credits [P7] [D7].
- **Platform rules a tool can check.**
  - YouTube chapters start at 00:00, need at least three, and each must be at least 10 s [D21].
  - Apple Podcasts asks for about −16 LKFS with a true peak at or below −1 dBFS [D22].
  - Spotify video podcasts want H.264, 16:9 and Rec.709 with stereo AAC, and HDR is tone-mapped to SDR [D23].
  - No platform publishes safe-zone figures, and third-party figures conflict [D24].
  - YouTube requires disclosure of realistic synthetic content but exempts colour fixes, background blur, captions and audio repair [D25].
- **Platforms build the simple cases themselves.** YouTube's own clips tool suggests moments only in 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Twitch is building vertical streaming (beta) and Auto Clips with captions (waitlist) [D26].

## The bets

The bets are ranked by how many creators each reaches, how often they would use it, and how far it puts Frame Job ahead rather than level, discounted by effort and risk.

Every bet has the same shape. Analysis that Frame Job already caches, or that macOS provides on the device, feeds a planner. The planner writes edits the core already knows how to make. Each result is therefore an ordinary undo step on a real timeline, and each command becomes an MCP tool that the Assistant and outside agents can run with no new agent work.

Effort is build effort (S, M, L, XL), never lines of code.

| Rank | Bet | Effort | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transcript tab | L | Everyone who records themselves talking |
| 2 | Screen recordings with the cursor as data | L | Screencasts, tutorials, courses, product demos |
| 3 | Make Vertical Version | M (copy), L (linked versions) | Everyone who posts shorts |
| 4 | Find Clips | M on top of 3 | Podcasters, long-form YouTubers, streamers |
| 5 | Switch by Speaker, and every audio track | M | Video podcasts and interviews |
| 6 | Camera cutout and layouts | L | Screencasters, talking heads, streamers |

Bets 1 and 2 remove the two points where talking creators and the home segment give up. Bets 3 and 4 complete the long-to-short loop. Bet 5 takes the podcast format on the strength of the audio chain. Bet 6 closes the presenter-camera gap.

### 1. Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review
### 2. Screen recordings with the cursor as data

**Pitch.** The recorder stops burning the pointer and click rings into the picture. Beside the movie it saves the cursor's path and image and every click. If the creator opts in, it also saves the shortcuts pressed. When the recording lands:

- zoom actions already sit on the action lane at each click and each burst of typing;
- the cursor is its own layer, which can be made bigger, restyled, smoothed or hidden when idle, and gets click ripples;
- each shortcut appears as a Keyboard keys overlay;
- long typing stretches can be sped up.

All of it is ordinary actions, clips and graphics that the creator can drag or delete. Recordings made before this ships, and imported screen videos, behave as today.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** The polished-screencast category rests on cursor data:

- Screen Studio zooms where clicks happened [S2] and edits the cursor after recording [S3];
- Prequel stores the pointer as data [S19];
- Cap [S16], FocuSee [S18], Tella [S11] and Camtasia [S8] [S9] do the same.

Frame Job's recorder stores none of it, so Frame Job loses its own home segment to a recorder that costs about $29 a month [S7]. This bet brings Frame Job level on polish. It pulls ahead because those recorders are shallow editors and Frame Job is a full one. Its auto zooms are actions on a real timeline, next to grading, the audio chain, captions and graphics, and an agent can re-plan them ("zoom only on the clicks in the settings pane").

Being free is not unique by itself. OpenScreen is a free, MIT-licensed Screen Studio alternative with about 40,000 stars, archived after v1.5.0 [S23], and Cap sells a $58 lifetime licence [S17].

**Builds on.** `RecordingSetup.swift`, which sets `showsCursor` and `showMouseClicks` today; `add_zoom_action` (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`); `add_speed_ramp`; the Keyboard keys graphic template; the recorder panel's grants; `recipe_layer.rs`; `MediaConsolidator` and relink.

**Effort.** L.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §11 (`recording.md`) decides three things this bet reverses: the cursor and click ring are taken as drawn and nothing is reconstructed; callouts stay out; a recording is ordinary media, with no source kind and no schema bump. The owner amends §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.
- Shortcuts need the Input Monitoring grant, which `RecorderStatusItem.swift` deliberately avoids today. Key capture should be opt-in and record only modifier shortcuts by default. It must never record secure fields, and it must show plainly when it is on.
- The cursor must follow the screen clip's own transform and zoom actions. It has to be drawn as part of that clip's layer, or the two have to be nested with the zooms on the nest. A sprite on another track would drift.
- `NSCursor.currentSystem` is marked deprecated in macOS 27.0 in Apple's availability metadata, so a replacement is needed.
- The sidecar cannot be regenerated, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it.
- Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame time, which the camera spike measured within 0.5 ms. Issue #370 is a microphone-offset problem and is not inherited.
- Motion blur on zooms needs sub-frame sampling and is out of scope.
- Code from AGPL-licensed recorders is not carried over, the same rule as for Concat.

### 3. Make Vertical Version

# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)

**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).

## Goal

Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
MCP mirror, as every control does today.

## What it delivers first

The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
limiter and the target.

## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)

Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
lanes, do so."

1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
   *Recommended.*
4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered
   offline as speed-ramp audio is. AP0's spike S1 confirms or overturns this. *Recommended.*
5. **One fixed chain order, not a user-ordered list.** Channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch
   → isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, each stage off by
   default and inert when off. A closed vocabulary like every other effect (§11 R5-1), and the
   order an engineer would choose for voice. *Recommended.*

Asked later, at the phase that needs them (each has a recommendation there): how the volume
line is edited (AP8), the split-edit model (AP9), track processing in the preview and the stem
format (AP10), and where speech spans live for ducking (AP11).

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Working arrangement:** this worktree is the integration branch; each phase is built
  through litecode in a lane of its own, gated, committed, rebased onto the integration branch
  one at a time and gated again there, as codec-export (CX-11) and grading (GR-25) merged
  phase by phase. Merging into main is done from the main checkout.
- **Lanes (the owner's "multiple lanes"):** after AP0, at most three at once, split by the
  files they touch. **Lane A, the voice block:** AP1 → AP2 → AP3 → AP4 → AP5 → AP6, then AP8
  and AP14, which build on its stages. **Lane B, editing and playback:** AP9 → AP13 → AP7
  (the meter after AP1 has landed, since both read `Loudness.swift`). **Lane C, the mix:**
  AP11 → AP10 (after AP2 has landed: both work in the export's float gain stage) → AP12
  (after AP3). A lane whose next phase waits on another lane's phase waits; it never builds
  against an unlanded one.
- **Collisions between lanes:** each phase numbers its decisions in its own block (APn's
  AU-n0…, AU-2's note), and a format bump is provisional until its phase lands: the
  integrator renumbers it (and its `schema_vN.rs`) when another lane landed one first.
- **Agent parity:** every new property is a `set_audio` key, every new command a tool, every
  new answer readable through `get_project`.
- **Proof currency:** exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic
  (`phase5_proof.py`'s BS.1770 and 4× true-peak oversampler), synthetic fixtures with known
  answers, and the owner's samples where present. What only ears can judge is a row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- **Samples:** the owner records the survey's §6 list. A phase uses a sample when it exists and
  a synthetic fixture otherwise; no phase waits for one.
- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults and bump the format (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older
  project opens unchanged and sounds the same.

## How it fits the tree (at `33eeed0`)

- **The clip strip runs in a tap, before the fader.** `AudioTap.swift` (595) puts one
  `MTAudioProcessingTap` (PreEffects) on each composition audio track and schedules each clip's
  settings by span (`AudioDSPSpan`). `AudioDSP.swift` (**890, over the cap**) holds pan, the mono
  fold, the compressor (default threshold −18 dB) and noise reduction, real-time safe. Volume,
  fades and ducking come after the tap, as the core's envelope played as volume ramps
  (`core/src/audio.rs` 537, `audio_duck.rs` 136). **A new live stage sees the clip at its
  recorded level**, so a level-relative stage (limiter, gate) must be told the clip's gain.
- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** One tap per input, already used by
  the meter (`LevelMeter.swift` 400, which sums per-track peaks as an upper bound, not the mix).
  The export measures a 32-bit float mix and gains it in `ExporterAudioGain.swift` (179); its
  write pass still decodes 16-bit integers (#86).
- **Offline renders have a pattern.** Speed-ramp audio renders into `cache/ramp-audio/` through
  `RampAudioRenders` (a serial queue, owners, a wait in the export, dry while pending).
- **Loudness exists once.** `Loudness.swift` (**674, over the cap**) is BS.1770-4 for the
  export; `ExporterLoudness.swift` (211) its measurement pass.
- **The model.** `AudioProps` lives in `core/src/model_props.rs` (551), checked by
  `props_check.rs` (526) and clamped by `actions_clamp.rs` (386); pan, mono, compressor, noise
  reduction, duck and keep pitch are BASE-only (`InspectorBinding+Writes.swift`'s
  `structural(audio:)`), and only volume, mute and the fades animate.
- **Caches.** Peaks, sync features and speech (Silero VAD) per media, on the cache lane
  (`MediaCacheLane.swift`); a loudness cache would be a fifth beside them.

## Phases

| Phase | Survey items | What a person gets |
|---|---|---|
| AP0 | — | Scope lifted, the spike's answers, the files split |
| AP1 | A2, A8 (readout) | A clip's LUFS shown; Normalize to a loudness |
| AP2 | A1, A13 | A true-peak limiter; the export reaches its loudness; 24-bit |
| AP3 | A3, A7, B7 | EQ and high-pass, hum removal, channel selection |
| AP4 | A5, A6 | Gate/expander, de-esser |
| AP5 | A4, B4 | Voice isolation; de-reverb if isolation does it |
| AP6 | B1, B3, B8 | Enhance Voice; the leveller; clean-up when a voice-over lands |
| AP7 | A8 | Live LUFS and true-peak meter |
| AP8 | A9 | Every audio parameter animates; the volume line on the clip |
| AP9 | A10 | J- and L-cuts that keep sync; reversible Detach |
| AP10 | A12, A11 | Track faders, track and master processing, stems |
| AP11 | B2, B9 | Ducking by speech; fade and crossfade shapes |
| AP12 | B6 | Match one clip's level and tone to another |
| AP13 | B5 | Audio while scrubbing |
| AP14 | B10 | Voice effects (E8, #123) |

AP1–AP6 are the voice block, in the order the owner's recording needs them. AP7 onward is the
mixing block and can be reordered freely; only AP12 needs AP3, and AP6 needs AP2–AP5.

### AP0 — scope, the record, the tolls and the spike

- **Decisions:** AU-2 (the scope, from choice 1), AU-3 (the chain, choices 4 and 5), AU-4 (the
  loudness defaults, choices 2 and 3). Spec §1's non-goal sentence rewritten; this road map
  opened.
- **Tolls, each a pure move landed and gated alone:** `AudioDSP.swift` cut at its MARKs (the
  compressor and noise reduction into their own files, the chain kept); `AudioTap.swift`'s
  schedule and parameters (its first two MARKs) out of the tap; `Loudness.swift` cut below the

- **Spike S, its rule fixed before its run, its record here:**

    band against the shipped noise reducer, and whether it reduces reverberation (B4's
    question), on a reverberant sample if one exists.
  - **S3 — tracks and the master in the preview.** Whether one composition audio track ever
    carries two timeline tracks; the error of a track chain run per composition track during an
    overlap (zero for linear stages, measured for dynamics); the options for a preview master
    limiter (none and say so, per-track, or an offline premix); rebuilding the true mix from the
    taps for a LUFS meter.
  - **S4 — a loudness cache.** K-weighted 100 ms block energies per media: size, build time on
    a 20-minute file, and integrated LUFS over any window against `Loudness.swift` measuring an
    export of the same window (agreement within 0.1 LU).
- **Acceptance:** `make gate` after each toll; the spike's verdicts recorded here.

### AP1 — loudness you can see and target (A2, A8's readout)

- A per-media loudness cache (`cache/loudness/<id>.bin`, S4's format) on the cache lane after
  peaks, current by `CacheStamp` like the others.
- The Volume section reads the clip's integrated loudness (gated, over the window that plays)
  and its true peak beside the Gain row.
- Normalize gains a **Loudness** mode: a target in LUFS, each clip of a selection to the same
  target, which is what "match these clips" means. Until AP2, a clip whose peak would pass the
  ceiling stops short and says where it landed, as the volume ceiling does today.
  `normalize_clip` gains `mode` and `target_lufs`.
- **Proof:** exports of normalised fixtures measured by the proof's BS.1770 within ±0.5 LU;
  the owner's recording; a selection of two levels landing equal.

### AP2 — limiters, and an export that reaches its loudness (A1, A13)

- A **clip limiter** stage in the tap: lookahead, 4× oversampled true-peak detection, a ceiling
  in dBTP. Because the fader is downstream, the stage is told the clip's gain (decision AU-n:
  the base volume, with fades and ducks only ever lowering it), and its lookahead is a lead
  like noise reduction's (SY-25).
- The **export:** a float decode before the gain (#86, closing it), a master limiter in the
  float write pass so the loudness target limits instead of capping, and an `audio_bits` choice
  of 16 or 24 on WAV and AIFF.
- Loudness Normalize uses the clip limiter, so the owner's recording reaches −16 LUFS at
  −1 dBTP. If choice 2 says so, Loudness becomes the button's default here.
- **Proof:** every export's true peak at or under its ceiling by the proof's oversampler; the
  loudness target met within ±0.5 LU on `phase5_proof.py`'s crest fixture, which today lands
  quieter; a 24-bit file decoded with its low bits used; the owner's recording.
- **Manual check:** no pumping or distortion on speech and on music.
- **Built in two parts, by size.** Part 1: the clip limiter, `audio.limiter` (format 30), its
  Limiter section and `set_audio` key, and Loudness Normalize through it as the default
  (AU-20…AU-26; its record below). Part 2: the export's float decode (#86), the master limiter
  in the float write pass and `audio_bits` (AU-27 on).

### AP3 — EQ, hum removal and channel selection (A3, A7, B7)

- **EQ:** a high-pass with a slope, a low-pass, low and high shelves and a number of parametric
  bands (set at AP3), with voice presets (rumble cut, de-mud, presence). An EQ section in the
  Sound sub-tab with the response curve drawn.
- **Hum:** notches at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, depth and harmonic count.
- **Channels:** both, left only, right only, swapped, before the mono fold, so a mic recorded
  on one channel of a stereo file plays at its level.
- **Model:** `audio.eq`, `audio.hum`, `audio.channels`; format bump; MCP keys.
- **Proof:** tones and sweeps through each band against the biquad's analytic response
  (±0.1 dB); notch depth at each harmonic; a channel pick sample-identical to its source channel.

### AP4 — gate, expander and de-esser (A5, A6)

- A downward **expander/gate** sharing the compressor's envelope follower: threshold relative
  to the clip's measured level (AP1), ratio, range, attack, hold, release.
- A **de-esser:** a compressor keyed on a high band (frequency, threshold, range).
- **Model, inspector, MCP** as AP3; format bump.
- **Proof:** a tone burst over noise, the pause floor lowered by the range and the burst
  untouched; sibilant noise bursts reduced in band and the voice band untouched; the owner's
  recording's pause floor.

### AP5 — voice isolation (A4; B4's verdict)

- **Isolation** by `AUSoundIsolation` (S2), rendered offline per clip window into
  `cache/isolated/` on the ramp-audio pattern: an Amount (wet/dry), dry while pending, the
  export waiting for its render, re-rendered when the window or the file changes.
- **De-reverb (B4):** if S2 measured reverberation removed, it is this control and the guide
  says so; otherwise B4 is filed with tier C and the measurement.
- **Proof:** the render aligned with the dry clip within a sample (cross-correlation); the pause
  floor and the speech band against the dry clip; dry while pending; an export that waits.
- **Manual check:** artefacts on the owner's voice at Amount 100 % and 50 %.

### AP6 — Enhance Voice, the leveller, and clean-up when a voice-over lands (B1, B3, B8)

- **Enhance Voice** (Clip menu, a button in the Sound sub-tab, an `enhance_voice` tool): reads
  the clip's loudness, its peak and the noise floor over the VAD cache's non-speech spans, then
  writes ORDINARY settings a person can see and change — high-pass, isolation or noise
  reduction, gate, de-esser if the high band is hot, a compressor set from the clip's own
  level, the limiter and the loudness target. One undo step; pressing it twice changes nothing.
- **Leveller (B3):** a slow gain-rider stage for a speaker who moves on and off the mic, off by
  default, turned on by Enhance Voice when the speech's short-term loudness range calls for it.
- **At record time (B8):** a recorder setting, "Enhance the microphone when it lands", applying
  Enhance Voice to the Microphone clip after the landing, as its own undo step (AU-68).
- **Proof:** the owner's recording to −16 LUFS ±0.5 at −1 dBTP with its pause floor lowered;
  idempotence; one undo step; a voice-over that lands enhanced.
- **Built in three parts, by size, as AP2 was.** Part 1: Enhance Voice itself — the measurements,
  the rules, the loudness cache's high band (version 2), the volume solved on the clip rendered
  through its own chain for Enhance and Loudness Normalize alike (the owner's answer,
  2026-10-31), the Measuring Sound sheet, the button, Clip ▸ Enhance Voice and `enhance_voice`
  (AU-60…AU-65; its record below). Part 2: the leveller, `audio.leveller` (a format bump) — after the
  owner's answer of 2026-10-31 a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's loudness and
  speech and applied with no state in the tap — its section, and Enhance turning it on from the
  speech's short-term loudness range (AU-66, AU-67; its record below). Part 3:
  "Enhance the microphone when it lands", the recorder setting and its `UserDefaults` key,
  applied after the landing as its own undo step (AU-68, AU-69; its record below).

### AP7 — live loudness and true-peak metering (A8)

- Momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and true peak while playing, over the true mix
  (S3's method), with a reset; the per-clip readout is AP1's.
- **Proof:** a probe compiled from `app/Sources` fed EBU Tech 3341's test signals, each within
  its tolerance.

### AP8 — every audio parameter animates; the volume line (A9)

Built in two parts once the owner answered the question below with (a), actions (2026-10-30,
AU-80): **AP8a** the volume line, app-only (AU-80…AU-84); **AP8b** every other audio parameter as
action ends through the same model (AU-85…).

- **AP8b:** pan, EQ gains and frequencies, gate, de-esser, compressor and limiter settings,
  isolation's Amount and the leveller's target as action ends; the tap's schedule carries
  per-parameter ramps from the core, not one constant per span. Switches (a stage on or off)
  still change at an action's end, as booleans do (§5.4).
- **AP8a, the volume line:** each clip draws its envelope over its waveform; dragging it edits the
  level. **Asked at AP8:** edit through actions (a point is an action's end, which keeps §2's
  "Actions, not keyframes"; recommended) or add keyframes (lifting it). Answered (a).
- **Proof:** the line drawn where the plan's ramps are (AP8a); exports of an animated pan and EQ
  against analytic gains (AP8b).

### AP9 — split edits (A10)

- J- and L-cuts that keep sync, and Detach Audio made reversible (Attach Audio).
- **Asked at AP9:** a LINKED pair — Detach's two clips carrying one link id, moved, cut and
  deleted together, with ⌥-drag trimming one half alone (recommended: it fits one kind of
  track, and an audio lead on its own track cannot collide with "overlap is a transition") —
  or one clip whose audio window extends past its picture.
- **Proof:** core tests of every edit on a linked pair; exports with the audio leading and
  trailing the picture by a known amount.

### AP10 — tracks, buses and stems (A12, A11)

- A **track fader and pan** in the header and the Track menu (an envelope term in the core, as
  a track's mute is).
- **Track and master processing** by S3's verdict, asked at AP10: the master limiter in the
  export at least; in the preview, as S3 found possible, or said plainly where it differs.
- **Stems:** each track, or a chosen set, as its own file in one export; **asked at AP10:**
  separate files (recommended) or a multitrack movie if S3 measured it to work.
- **Proof:** fader arithmetic on an export; the stems summed against the full mix (a null within
  quantisation when no master dynamics run).

### AP11 — ducking by speech, and fade shapes (B2, B9)

- **Ducking by speech:** the ducking clip's speech spans from the VAD cache, with pre-roll, hold
  and release, drawn as the envelope it makes. **Asked at AP11:** spans persisted on the media
  (a detected field, as Camera Log's is; recommended, so the plan stays a function of the
  project) or handed to the plan by the host.
- **Fade and crossfade shapes:** linear, S-curve, +3 dB and −3 dB, sampled by the core like an
  eased action.
- **Proof:** the plan's ramps against fixture spans; exports of each fade shape against its
  formula.

### AP12 — match one clip to another (B6)

- **Match Loudness** to a reference clip (AP1's measurement) and **Match EQ:** the reference's
  and the target's average speech spectra fitted to AP3's bands. A command and a tool.
- **Proof:** pink noise tilted by a known EQ matched back within ±1 dB a band.

### AP13 — audio while scrubbing (B5)

- Short grains of the mix at the scrub position while the playhead is dragged, off when the
  drag stops; the design is set at AP13 against what AVFoundation allows.
- **Proof:** a probe of the grain scheduler. **Manual check:** the feel, and no clicks.

### AP14 — voice effects (B10, E8)

- E8 as designed and measured (`designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, #123): sixteen kinds as fixed
  chains of Apple units rendered offline, with an amount and a pitch. Closes #123.

### AP0's record (2026-10-30)

**Landed.** `9e47f56`: the survey, this plan, AU-2…AU-4 and spec §1's audio non-goal lifted. The
tolls, each a pure move gated alone (PASS 307, 246, 243 and 136 s) and checked line-identical

`AudioNoiseReductionStage.swift` 376), `54e4649` (`AudioTap.swift` 595 → 328;

     5	/// The half of screen recording a probe can call: values in, values out, no
     6	/// framework object that needs a bundle (road map 3, R1a). What a recording
     7	/// IS before it starts — the choice, where its files go, the two
     8	/// ScreenCaptureKit configurations built from that choice, and the two
     9	/// grants it stands on — so that `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` can read
    10	/// every field back from a bare Mach-O that never starts a stream.
    11	///
    12	/// `ScreenRecorder.swift` (with `+Pause.swift`, `+Microphone.swift`,
    13	/// `+Finishing.swift`, `+Delegates.swift` and `+Content.swift`) is the other
    14	/// half: the class that owns the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per
    15	/// SEGMENT (R2: a pause removes one and a resume adds the next) and, when a
    16	/// microphone is chosen, the `AVCaptureSession` for the second file. The
    17	/// result types a recording ends as — `StopReason`, `RecordingSegment`,
    18	/// `RecordingResult`, `RecorderError` — are `RecordingResult.swift`, moved
    19	/// off the foot of this file at the 400-line cap; they are still values a
    20	/// probe can make.
    21	///
    22	/// Three R0 facts shape the configuration and are restated on the fields
    23	/// they decide (`archive/roadmap-3.md`, "R0 — the answers"):
    24	///
    25	/// - **The microphone is a second file** (q2). `captureMicrophone` on the
    26	///   stream writes ONE stereo track that is the SUM of system and microphone
    27	///   sound, which is decision 5's bad case — so `make` never sets it, and
    28	///   `RecordingChoice.microphone` names an `AVCaptureDevice` for
    29	///   `ScreenRecorder`'s capture session instead.
    30	/// - **`.best` does not scale by itself** (q4). `captureResolution = .best`
    31	///   at the display's point size writes a point-sized file; pixels come only
    32	///   when `width`/`height` are asked for in pixels, so `make` multiplies the
    33	///   point size by the display's backing scale under `.best` itself.
    34	/// - **Show Clicks needs BGRA** (q6a). `SCStream.h` says `showMouseClicks`
    35	///   "currently applies when pixelFormat is set to BGRA" and a fresh
    36	///   configuration reads `420v`, so `make` sets `REDACTED`
    37	///   when clicks are on and leaves the default alone otherwise — measured, a
    38	///   recording output over a BGRA stream starts and writes.
    39	
    40	// MARK: - The choice
    41	
    42	/// What is recorded. `.picked` is the panel's picker result, whose filter
    43	/// is carried beside the choice (`ScreenRecorder.start` takes the filter as
    44	/// its own argument), so the source enum never holds a framework object.
    45	/// `.voiceOver` is the microphone alone, no picture (spec §11 recording, #99):
    46	/// `ScreenRecorder.startVoiceOver` records it and `start` refuses it.
    47	/// `.camera` is a camera alone, the device in `RecordingChoice.camera` (spec
    48	/// §11 CAM-3): `ScreenRecorder.startCamera` records it and `start` refuses it,
    49	/// while `start` records a camera beside a display, window or picked source (CAM-9).
    50	enum RecordingSource: Equatable {
    51	    case display(CGDirectDisplayID)
    52	    case window(CGWindowID)
    53	    case picked
    54	    case voiceOver
    55	    case camera
    56	}
    57	
    58	/// `nominal` records the display's POINT size, `best` its pixel size
    59	/// (`RecordingConfiguration.make` does the multiply — R0 q4).
    60	enum RecordingResolution: String, CaseIterable {
    61	    case nominal
    62	    case best
    63	}
    64	
    65	/// Where the recording lands when it stops. `.document` carries the target's
    66	/// `recipeKey` rather than an `ObjectIdentifier`: an identifier of a closed
    67	/// document is reused by the next one at the same address
    68	/// (`RelinkSheetController.swift` says so), while a `recipeKey` is never

   122	    static func folder() -> URL {

   138	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
   139	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
   140	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
   141	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {

   143	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
   144	        formatter.timeZone = .current

   151	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
   152	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
   153	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
   154	        formatter.timeZone = .current
   155	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"

   202	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
   203	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
   204	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
   205	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
   206	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
   207	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
   208	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
   209	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
   210	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
   211	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
   212	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
   213	    static func make(
   214	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
   215	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
   216	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
   217	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
   218	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
   219	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
   220	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
   221	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
   222	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
   223	        stream.showsCursor = true
   224	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks
   225	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
   226	        // is left alone when clicks are off, so an ordinary recording's
   227	        // pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
   228	        if choice.showClicks { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
   229	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
   230	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
   231	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
   232	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
   233	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
   234	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
   235	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
   236	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
   237	
   238	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
   239	        output.outputURL = outputURL
   240	        output.outputFileType = .mov
   241	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
   242	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
   243	        output.videoCodecType =
   244	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
   245	        return (stream, output)
   246	    }
   247	}
   248	
   249	// MARK: - The grants
   250	
   251	/// Decision 4 (road map 3 §0): the PANEL asks for the grants, the tool never
   252	/// does — the rule the speech grant's `canAsk` carried, for two grants.
   253	/// What lives here is the READ of each grant, the STEP a press takes, the
   254	/// pane URLs and the sentences — all pure: nothing here prompts or opens;
   255	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()`, `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess` and
   256	/// the pane's `NSWorkspace.open` are called by the recorder panel alone
   257	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Grants.swift`), because a system prompt needs
   258	/// a person in front of it. A press asks for Screen Recording ONCE and
   259	/// opens the pane on every later press (spec §11 recording) — but only in
   260	/// a launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks, because TCC
   261	/// gives that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1). A denied or restricted
   262	/// microphone opens its pane; `.notDetermined` asks.
   263	///
   264	/// **Both refusal sentences are COMPUTED, and end with `launchClause` when
   265	/// it is non-empty** (R1 review, unjudged and upheld): R0 q1 measured that
   266	/// a shell-launched Frame Job is attributed by TCC to the TERMINAL, so a
   267	/// person who followed the pane sentence and granted Frame Job.app would have
   268	/// granted the wrong application and be refused again with no way to tell
   269	/// why. The pane sentence stays the PREFIX — `recording_proof.py` matches
   270	/// on it — and the clause names the launching process's pid.
   271	enum RecordingGrant {
   272	    /// `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` — true when this PROCESS may
   273	    /// capture. R0 q1: a shell-launched binary is attributed by TCC to the
   274	    /// terminal, so from a proof this reads the terminal's grant, not the
   275	    /// app's.
   276	    static var screenRecordingGranted: Bool { CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess() }
   277	
   278	    /// The pane sentence alone — the prefix of `screenRecordingRefusal`.
   279	    static let screenRecordingPaneSentence =
   280	        "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ "
   281	        + "Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch."
   282	
   283	    static var screenRecordingRefusal: String { screenRecordingPaneSentence + launchClause }
   284	
   285	    /// Empty for an app launched by launchd (`open -a`, the Finder, the
   286	    /// Dock — ppid 1, responsible for itself); otherwise the sentence that
   287	    /// says whose grant this process is actually running under. `getppid()`
   288	    /// is the cheapest true reading: R0 q1's `responsibility_get_pid_
   289	    /// responsible_for_pid` is private API, and the parent is what TCC
   290	    /// follows for a process launched from a shell.
   291	    static var launchClause: String {
   292	        let parent = getppid()
   293	        guard parent != 1 else { return "" }
   294	        return " This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid \(parent)), so the grant "
   295	            + "that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or "
   296	            + "relaunch with open -a \"Frame Job\"."
   297	    }
   298	
   299	    /// `AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus(for: .audio)`. Read BEFORE any
   300	    /// `AVCaptureDeviceInput` is made: that initializer auto-prompts on
   301	    /// `.notDetermined`, which is exactly the prompt the tool may not put up.
   302	    static var microphoneStatus: AVAuthorizationStatus {
   303	        AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus(for: .audio)
   304	    }
   305	
   306	    /// The status as the framework spells it, for a message a script can
   307	    /// read — `Transcriber.name(of:)`'s shape.
   308	    static func name(of status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
   309	        switch status {
   310	        case .notDetermined: return "notDetermined"
   311	        case .restricted: return "restricted"
   312	        case .denied: return "denied"
   313	        case .authorized: return "authorized"
   314	        @unknown default: return "unknown"
   315	        }
   316	    }
   317	
   318	    /// Names the status word and the one action that changes it: a
   319	    /// `notDetermined` grant is asked for by pressing Record in the panel (the
   320	    /// only place that may prompt), a denied or restricted one is turned on
   321	    /// in System Settings. `launchClause` follows, on the same terms as the
   322	    /// screen sentence's.
   323	    static func microphoneRefusal(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
   324	        let head = "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: \(name(of: status))). "
   325	        switch status {
   326	        case .notDetermined:
   327	            return head + "Press Record in File ▸ New Recording… once to grant it." + launchClause
   328	        default:
   329	            return head + "Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, "
   330	                + "then relaunch." + launchClause
   331	        }
   332	    }
   333	
   334	    // MARK: The step a press takes
   335	
   336	    /// What a press of Record does about one grant: go on, put up the
   337	    /// system prompt, or open System Settings at the grant's pane.
   338	    enum Step: Equatable {
   339	        case proceed
   340	        case ask
   341	        case openPane
   342	    }
   343	
   344	    /// True when launchd is the parent (`open -a`, the Finder, the Dock) —
   345	    /// the reading `launchClause` makes, so the two cannot disagree.
   346	    static var launchedByLaunchd: Bool { getppid() == 1 }
   347	
   348	    /// Screen Recording: granted goes on; a shell launch always asks (its
   349	    /// prompt is the terminal's, R0 q1, so `asked` means nothing there);
   350	    /// a launchd-owned press that has asked before opens the pane; else ask.
   351	    static func screenStep(granted: Bool, asked: Bool, launchedByLaunchd: Bool) -> Step {
   352	        if granted { return .proceed }
   353	        if !launchedByLaunchd { return .ask }
   354	        if asked { return .openPane }
   355	        return .ask
   356	    }
   357	
   358	    /// The microphone, when one is chosen: authorized goes on,
   359	    /// `.notDetermined` asks, and denied, restricted or unknown opens the
   360	    /// pane — the system never prompts twice for it.
   361	    static func microphoneStep(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> Step {
   362	        switch status {
   363	        case .authorized: return .proceed
   364	        case .notDetermined: return .ask
   365	        case .denied, .restricted: return .openPane
   366	        @unknown default: return .openPane
   367	        }
   368	    }
   369	
   370	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording.
   371	    static let screenRecordingPaneURL = URL(
   372	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture")
   373	
   374	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone.
   375	    static let microphonePaneURL = URL(
   376	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Microphone")
   377	
   378	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera (camera-recording CR1c).
   379	    static let cameraPaneURL = URL(
   380	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Camera")
   381	
   382	    /// What a note adds once the pane has been opened.
   383	    static let paneOpenedSentence = " System Settings is open at that pane."
   384	
   385	    /// The screen note after the pane opened: the pane sentence stays the
   386	    /// PREFIX, and `launchClause` stays last.
   387	    static var screenRecordingOpenedNote: String {
   388	        screenRecordingPaneSentence + paneOpenedSentence + launchClause
   389	    }
   390	
   391	    /// The microphone note after its pane opened: the refusal's head and
   392	    /// fix, the opened sentence, then `launchClause`.
   393	    static func microphoneOpenedNote(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
   394	        "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: \(name(of: status))). "
   395	            + "Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, then relaunch."
   396	            + paneOpenedSentence + launchClause
   397	    }
   398	}

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Screen recording (road map 3)
     2	
     3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
     4	[`README.md`](README.md).
     5	
     6	- **Screen recording is IN; camera recording and callouts stay OUT** (road
     7	  map 3, reversing §1's day-one non-goal). A screen recording is the input
     8	  the whole product was shaped around; camera capture is a second capture
     9	  stack and callouts are a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant.
    10	  What ScreenCaptureKit draws into the pixels for free — the cursor, and
    11	  a ring around each click — is taken; nothing is reconstructed afterwards.
    12	  **Amended by CAM-1** (camera recording, CR0): camera recording is now IN
    13	  — a camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and
    14	  track, through this recorder's panel (`camera-recording.md`); callouts
    15	  stay OUT.
    16	- **A recording is ordinary media.** The recorder writes a file and the app
    17	  imports it through exactly the path File ▸ Open and Add Media… use
    18	  (`adoptImported`, the two-try placement). The model learns nothing: no
    19	  source kind, no flag, no schema bump. Every op, cache and export treats a
    20	  recording clip as the media clip it is.
    21	- **The file lives in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`**, named by date and
    22	  time, never in the package and never in the temporary directory: an
    23	  untitled document has no package (§5.6), and a recording is ORIGINAL
    24	  footage, so the one place it may not go is where a cache is regenerable.
    25	  Consolidate carries it in on the same terms as any other file.
    26	  `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides the folder for a proof.
    27	  **Amended by NM-4** (rename R0): `~/Movies/Reelcut Recordings/` is now
    28	  `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`.
    29	- **The canvas takes the recorder's RATE; the media record takes the
    30	  file's.** ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when the screen changes,
    31	  so its files are variable-rate and the probe honestly reports something
    32	  like 24981/1000 (measured); the untitled document is built at the 30 or
    33	  60 the panel asked for, because that is the grid the person chose, and
    34	  `set_canvas` is NOT used for it afterwards — an untitled document's
    35	  first project is not an undo step, and the rate is part of what the
    36	  document IS.
    37	- **The panel asks for the grants; the tool never does.** `Transcriber`'s
    38	  rule for two grants: Screen Recording (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`
    39	  reads, `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` asks) and Microphone
    40	  (`AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus`, `requestAccess`). The microphone
    41	  status is read BEFORE any `AVCaptureDeviceInput` is constructed, because
    42	  that initializer prompts on its own. `record_screen` reads and refuses by
    43	  name with the fix in the sentence. The built app needs BOTH the plist
    44	  usage key and the hardened-runtime entitlement
    45	  `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` for the microphone; Screen
    46	  Recording needs neither.
    47	- **A press of Record asks for Screen Recording once, and every later
    48	  press opens System Settings at the pane** (2026-09-28). The first press
    49	  without the grant calls `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess`, and the panel
    50	  remembers it across launches in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`, because
    51	  the system prompt appears once per app, not once per launch; every later
    52	  press opens `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture`
    53	  through `NSWorkspace` and the note says System Settings is open at that
    54	  pane (the plain refusal when `open` answers false). The flag counts only
    55	  in a launchd-owned launch (`getppid() == 1`, `launchClause` empty): a
    56	  shell-launched press always asks and never writes it, because TCC gives
    57	  that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1), and a flag written there would stop
    58	  a later Finder launch from ever being put in the pane's list. A
    59	  `.denied` or `.restricted` microphone opens `Privacy_Microphone` the same
    60	  way; `.notDetermined` still asks, and a prompt's answer never opens
    61	  Settings. Only the panel opens a pane: `record_screen` never does, and
    62	  opening Settings is no edit and gets no mirror. Measured on macOS 26.5.1
    63	  (25F80): System Settings is the default handler of
    64	  `x-apple.systempreferences`; `SecurityPrivacyExtension.appex` declares
    65	  `legacyBundleIdentifier` `com.apple.preference.security` with
    66	  `allowsXAppleSystemPreferencesURLScheme` true, and its binary holds
    67	  `Privacy_ScreenCapture` and `Privacy_Microphone`. Accepted: the flag is
    68	  never cleared, so after `tccutil reset ScreenCapture` a launchd-owned
    69	  press opens the pane rather than prompting (the pane's + adds the app).
    70	  Whether the pane lands on its row is a person's check (REC-1, REC-2 in
    71	  `docs/manual-checks.md`). **Before either prompt, and before opening a
    72	  pane, the panel steps down from `.floating` to `.normal`**: a floating
    73	  panel sits over every normal window on the screen, and the prompt and
    74	  System Settings are another process's normal windows — the person found
    75	  the Screen Recording prompt hidden behind the panel. The next press that
    76	  goes on, a granted microphone's answer, and `show()` float it again.
    77	  **Amended by NM-6** (rename R0): `ReelcutScreenRecordingAsked` is now
    78	  `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`.
    79	- **Microphone and system audio are two sources and stay two FILES.**
    80	  Measured (road map 3's R0): with both on, `SCRecordingOutput` writes ONE
    81	  stereo track that is their SUM, inseparable and clipping when both are
    82	  loud — the one thing a screencast cutter cannot repair afterwards. So the
    83	  microphone is never on the recording stream; it is an `AVCaptureSession`
    84	  writing its own `.m4a` beside the movie, started first in the same
    85	  run-loop turn, and it lands as its own clip on its own track at the
    86	  offset the two did-start callbacks measured (a per-SEGMENT number since
    87	  R2 — R0 q7 measured a different one at every resume — never a constant).
    88	- **Undo of Add Recording leaves the files on disk**, exactly as undoing Add
    89	  Media… does. A recorder that deleted footage on ⌘Z would be the only
    90	  destructive undo in the app. For a recording that opened as a new project
    91	  the first segment IS the document and has no step; the rest is one step,
    92	  Add Microphone (one segment, with any voice — its own or a left-out
    93	  segment's) or Add Recording Segments.
    94	- **A paused recording is a SEQUENCE of files over ONE stream** (road map
    95	  3's R2, 2026-09-12). ScreenCaptureKit has no pause: the only lever is
    96	  removing the recording output — its file closes — and adding a fresh one
    97	  to a new file while the stream keeps capturing, measured (R0 q7) at
    98	  5–25 ms to close, 8–10 ms to start and 57 fps through the pause; the
    99	  microphone's writer is stopped and restarted per segment on its one
   100	  session. Each segment is named by its OWN start time, carries its own
   101	  measured offset, and lands as a clip touching the previous one; the model
   102	  still learns nothing, and nothing joins the files afterwards.
   103	- **The recorder panel goes away when a recording starts, for every
   104	  source, and comes back only with something to say** (R2). The menu bar's
   105	  status item is the recording's chrome — Pause Recording and Stop
   106	  Recording, then Resume Recording and Stop Recording while paused; File ▸
   107	  Pause Recording is a second door to pause (below) — and the panel returns
   108	  after the landing only when it was on screen as the recording began and
   109	  the landing's note is non-empty (a stop from the SYSTEM's own indicator —
   110	  Frame Job's item's Stop writes no note — a closed target, a segment left
   111	  out as unreadable, a microphone problem, a refused resume, a file the
   112	  landing could not place, a failure). ⌥⌘N shows it again; while it is
   113	  hidden, the quit guard opens the item's menu rather than beeping.
   114	  A voice-over (Microphone Only) is the exception: the panel stays up
   115	  (2026-10-02; "A voice-over is a recording with no picture", below).
   116	- **The recorder panel takes key only from an active Frame Job** (#137,
   117	  2026-09-29). Shown with Frame Job active (File ▸ New Recording…, ⌥⌘N, the
   118	  welcome button), it comes to the front key, with Record on Return. Shown
   119	  with Frame Job in the background (a script's `perform_menu_item`, a Dock
   120	  quit while a tool records), it is ordered front without key: Frame Job
   121	  stays inactive, and the person's typing, Return included, stays in the
   122	  app in front. A click on it still works without activating Frame Job
   123	  (`.nonactivatingPanel`).
   124	- **A segment whose movie will not probe is left out** (#97, 2026-09-29).
   125	  The walker that probes a finished recording's segments skips it and goes
   126	  on; the result's `unreadable`, and the landing's note at both doors (the
   127	  panel's and `record_screen`'s), name it and the files it kept on disk.
   128	  Only a recording with NO readable movie fails: the first segment's error,
   129	  `namingFiles` naming every file, so one segment reads byte for byte as
   130	  before. A segment whose recording output reports a FAILURE after its
   131	  `stoppedAt` was set (a pause's or the stop's) is left out the same way
   132	  (#181, 2026-09-30): the failure is that segment's, the recording goes on
   133	  or finishes, and the walker leaves it out UNPROBED with the writer's
   134	  sentence as its `unreadable` reason. Only a did-fail for the segment
   135	  still recording (no `stoppedAt`) is the recording's failure. A
   136	  microphone failure the machine asked for — the segment's
   137	  `stoppedAt` set: a pause's or the stop's did-finish, e.g. −11805 for a
   138	  writer stopped before its first sample — is that segment's `micProblem`
   139	  only; `microphoneProblem`, the live note, is a microphone that dies
   140	  MID-segment.
   141	- **A left-out segment's readable microphone lands without its picture**
   142	  (#181 item 2, 2026-10-01). When a segment is left out, the walker still
   143	  probes its microphone file, unless that segment's mic writer reported its
   144	  own failure (`micFailure`). A file that reads travels on the
   145	  `UnreadableSegment` with `position`, its place among the landed segments.
   146	  The landing puts the voice in its picture's SLOT: on the Microphone track,
   147	  at the point the picture sequence had reached, with offset 0 (there is no
   148	  picture to align it to), floored at the previous voice's end and
   149	  head-trimmed by the existing rule. The slot's length is the file's length
   150	  snapped down to the frame; the picture track stays empty for that
   151	  stretch, and the next picture starts at the slot's end, so later
   152	  segments keep their timing against their own voices. In a NEW project
   153	  the first readable segment is the document at 0, so a voice left out
   154	  before it lands as media only, with a sentence naming its file. The
   155	  left-out segment's own sentence is unchanged (it is also said when the
   156	  landing fails); only a landing that succeeded adds "The left-out
   157	  segment's microphone, <path>, was added to the project without its
   158	  picture." — the panel's note after the unreadable sentence, the tool's
   159	  `note` between the unreadable and microphone notes — and a failed landing
   160	  never says it. The tool's `unreadable` entry gains `mic_path` and
   161	  `mic_duration`, and `mic_media` and `mic_clip` when known; the panel
   162	  selects the voice's clip. The voice is part of the same grouped edit: Add
   163	  Recording, or in a new project Add Microphone when the document has one
   164	  segment and Add Recording Segments otherwise. **With NO readable movie
   165	  the recording still FAILS**, even when a microphone reads: a
   166	  `RecordingResult` is never empty of segments, and its `descriptor`,
   167	  `startedAt`, `filesClause` and `untitled(around:)` are the first
   168	  segment's picture, so a voice-only result would be a new result shape
   169	  through the walker, both doors and the landing. The voice is not lost:
   170	  the failure deletes no file, and `namingFiles` names every movie and then
   171	  every microphone file on disk — the microphone files alone ("The
   172	  microphone is at …") when no movie is on disk at all — so the person can
   173	  import it. A left-out segment whose voice does not read takes no time, as
   174	  before.
   175	- **File ▸ Pause Recording** (#98, 2026-09-29). Directly under New
   176	  Recording…, retitled Resume Recording from the RECORDER's state, enabled

# Spec §11 — decisions: Camera recording (road map "camera-recording")

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed (2026-10-27): its condensed record is
`designs/adr/camera-recording.md`, the original `archive/camera-recording.md`. Its parent design
is road map 3 (`designs/adr/roadmap-03-screen-recording.md`), whose decisions in
[`recording.md`](recording.md) stand unless an entry here amends one. CAM-7 onwards are in
[`camera-recording-2.md`](camera-recording-2.md), split from this file at the close by the
spec's ~500-line rule; the IDs are one series. CAM-1 and CAM-2 were recorded in CR0, before any
product code and before the spike's measured run. Each later phase recorded its rule in this
series (CAM-3 on), before its code.

- **CAM-1 — Camera recording is IN; callouts stay OUT** (the owner, 2026-10-26, reversing the
  camera half of recording.md's first bullet and §1's non-goal). Frame Job records a camera on
  its own, or at the same time as a screen recording (a talking head over a screencast). The
  owner's four answers, as given:
  1. **Camera alone, or camera at the same time as a screen recording.** Each capture lands as
     its own file on its own track. With a screen recording the camera goes on a track ABOVE
     the screen, placed as a corner picture-in-picture that can be moved; the corner, the scale
     and the inset are CR3's to decide.
  2. **The entry is the existing recorder panel**: a Camera source, and a camera row when
     recording the screen. One panel, one countdown, one menu-bar status item with Pause and
     Stop, the same landing into the project. File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) stays the one door.
  3. **Devices**: built-in and USB/UVC cameras and iPhone Continuity Camera; a live preview of
     the chosen camera in the panel; a choice of resolution and frame rate from the camera's
     formats, otherwise its best format.
  4. **Audio**: the chosen microphone (which can be the camera's own) is its own audio file on
     its own track, lined up to the picture, as screen recording does today.

  Everything else recording.md decided carries over: a recording is ordinary media, the files
  live in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, the panel asks for the grants and the tool never
  does, the microphone is a second file, a pause is a sequence of files, one grouped edit lands
  everything, and every door has an MCP mirror (a new source is an argument of `record_screen`,
  the voice-over's precedent, unless a phase records otherwise). Callouts stay out for the
  reason recording.md gives: a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant. **Risk
  accepted:** a second capture stack (`AVCaptureSession` for a camera) beside ScreenCaptureKit,
  a Camera grant and its entitlement, and a camera's own clock to line up with the screen's and
  the microphone's; CR0 measures each before any of it is built.

- **CAM-2 — The camera spike's rule (CR0), fixed before its run.** `tools/proof/camera_spike/`
  measures camera capture alone and beside a running screen recording; `results.json` stores
  this file's SHA-256 as `rule_sha256`, so the rule a recorded run read is pinned. The VERDICT
  line reads `VERDICT writer=<movie-output|asset-writer|STOP> screen_start=<E1|E2|STOP>
  continuity_key=<needed|not-needed|unmeasured> camera_entitlement=<needed|not-needed|unmeasured>
  best_format=<per-device summary>`, or `VERDICT NOT MEASURED: <reason>` when every `write` row
  is skipped.

content.content:
7. **During a recording.** A camera taken away during a recording ends it (CAM-3,
     unchanged); its list change applies at idle.

- **CAM-9 — A camera beside the screen (CR3a), recorded before its code.** `ScreenRecorder.start`
  with a display, window or picked source and `choice.camera` set also records the camera: one
  `(Camera).mov` per segment beside the screen's movie, paused and resumed with it, each placed
  against the screen by E2 (CAM-2's second estimator). The result carries the camera's files and
  offsets. CAM-3's files, codec and warm-up, CAM-5 (5)'s take and CAM-7 (7)'s adopt rule stand.
  1. **The start.** The order is `.busy`, the source guards, Screen Recording, then the Camera
     grant (read, never asked). Then the camera lookup ("No camera with the id … is
     connected.", `.cameraDevice`) and its format (`chosenFormat`, CAM-6 (3)). Then the
     Microphone grant and device, the folder, the recording output, the `.screen` frame watch
     (a throw is `.startFailed`) and the microphone capture. The camera is taken LAST
     (`takeCameraCapture(…, adopting: mayAsk)`, CAM-5 (5), CAM-7 (7)); a throw there stops an
     adopted microphone session and refuses. Without a camera `start` is as before: no `.screen`
     output, the same order.
  2. **The warm-up comes before the stream.** The state is `.arming` while the capture starts or
     joins its prepared start. On its answer ONE main turn runs `launchScreen`: the microphone
     file's `startRecording` (when a microphone was chosen), then `stream.startCapture`, then
     segment 0's camera writer is armed (CR0: the order of the starts made no measurable
     difference). Without a camera `start` calls `launchScreen` in its own turn, so road map 3
     R0 q6b's order is kept. A camera that fails to start, or stops on its own while arming,
     fails the start with its `.cameraDevice` sentence. The arm ceiling covers the warm-up.
     `camera.note` is the warm-up's note.
  3. **E2.** The watch is on the stream only with a camera, built with two frame intervals at
     the recording's rate as its bound (`2 / rate` seconds: 33.3 ms at 60 fps; CR0's E2 fell
     9–22 ms after E1). It keeps the PTS (seconds, as delivered; CR0 measured them on the host
     clock) of every COMPLETE frame for 2 s. Each segment's did-start is stamped on the host
     clock where it arrives (E1). E2 is the first kept or later complete frame at or after E1
     and no more than the bound after it. A segment's question is dropped at its close (a pause,
     the finishing), so a frame of a later segment never answers it. No frame in that window, or
     none by the close, leaves E2 unset.
  4. **The offset** is the camera's first buffer's PTS (host clock) minus E2, else minus E1, in
     ticks; POSITIVE means the camera began after the screen. Without both host stamps it is the
     first buffer's arrival minus the screen's start (`screenStart(of:)`); without those, 0. A
     still screen sends no complete frame, so such a segment uses E1, as does a segment whose
     first complete frame came past the bound.
  5. **The files.** Each segment's camera is `<screen movie stem> (Camera).mov`, made unique as
     the microphone's file is, at the format (HEVC else H.264, CAM-3). A resume's candidate name
     is skipped when its camera file is held.
  6. **Pause and resume in step.** A pause closes the open segment's camera writer and drops its
     E2 question; a resume arms the next writer after its output is added. **The watch comes off
     the stream for a resume's add** (measured at CR3a, amending this rule before its code). With
     the `.screen` output left on the running stream, every resumed segment's `SCRecordingOutput`
     reported "Failed due to failure to process first sample buffer" and wrote no movie, in 4 of
     4 runs of G16; without the output both segments landed in 3 of 3. So `resume()` removes the
     watch's `.screen` output BEFORE `addRecordingOutput` and adds it back once that add has
     returned, the new output started (`addRecordingOutput` "Starts Recording if stream is
     already capturing"). Measured so in a scratch copy, both segments landed in 2 of 2 runs,
     with E2 − E1 at 12.0 and 17.3 ms, then 19.7 and 21.5 ms. The pause leaves the watch on the

The screen recorder's microphone offset by callback arrival can differ from the files' startPTS offset by more than a frame
A screen recording places its microphone file by the offset between the two did-start callbacks (spec §11 `recording.md`, the "two FILES" bullet). The camera-recording spike (CR0, `tools/proof/camera_spike/`, 2026-10-26; record in `designs/camera-recording.md`, CR0 ▸ Record) measured that offset both ways, by callbacks and by `startPTS`, both on the host clock:

- With a camera movie output and a separate microphone session (M2, today's `microphoneSession` shape), the two offsets differ by 213.6 ms median (210.8–241.3, 3 runs). Most of that is the movie output's own −202 ms between its `startPTS` and its callback.
- With an asset writer and a microphone session (P2, the re-run on the final instrument), they differ by about 63 ms (+80.7 against +18.1 ms by `startPTS` and by callbacks).
- For the screen itself, the arrival of `recordingOutputDidStartRecording` (E1) was within 21 ms of the counter's truth in 16 runs, and E2 (the first `.screen` frame's PTS at or after it) within 0.5 ms.

Not measured: whether the screen recorder's microphone, placed by callbacks, is off by more than a frame against the screen file. The microphone's own `startPTS`-to-callback was not logged separately, and A1 (a person aiming the camera) is the only truth.

Next: log the microphone's `startPTS` on the host clock beside its callback in a screen recording, and move the offset to `startPTS` if they differ by more than a frame.
